summary: postinstall script exfiltrates host recon and credential-shaped env var names to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: package.json declares `postinstall: node dist/recon.js`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. The script in dist/recon.js collects hostname, username, SUDO_USER, home directory, cwd, platform/arch/release, internal network interface addresses, DNS domain (via `dnsdomainname`), CI indicators, and npm lifecycle metadata. It enumerates the full list of process environment variable names and additionally filters that list against a regex matching credential-shaped names (AWS, GCP, AZURE, NPM, NODE_AUTH, DOCKER, KUBE, VAULT, TOKEN, SECRET, KEY, PASS, CRED, GITHUB, GITLAB, SSH). The collected JSON body is POSTed over plain HTTP to http://138.68.108.20/cb. A header comment describes the script as "NON-SENSITIVE telemetry only" and claims env var names are never collected, contradicting the code's explicit credential-name filter and internal-network enumeration. Behavior is consistent with pre-attack reconnaissance of installer machines and build systems for supply-chain targeting.
